deep.reconstruction:
The page has no derivation. It holds lattice diagrams, a few short labels and pen trials. What follows describes them and offers a tentative interpretation.

(1) Top, headed '2h'. This is a square array of lattice points. Every other row consists of small circles alternating with dots, and the rows between are dots only. So the circles mark one sublattice, roughly the points with both coordinates even, inside the full integer lattice; read on the complex plane, a sublattice such as 2Z[i] inside Z[i]. Two nearly congruent triangles are drawn over it. Each has a long upper side running slightly downward to the right, a long left side going down to a bottom vertex, and a right side. The second triangle is the first shifted by about half a lattice step. Read with the next page (folio 34), the natural interpretation is lattice-point counting in a triangle. Folio 34 has the headings 'g+e', a square cut by a diagonal into regions A and B with the expression 5/8(p-1)+1/2(A-B), a 0/1 checkerboard (parity classes of lattice points), and the Gaussian integer 5+8i, of norm 89. The aim would be to compare how many points of each class (circles vs. dots) fall in a triangle and in its shifted copy. Such counts give Eisenstein/Gauss-lemma-type evaluations of a residue character, here plausibly a biquadratic character modulo a Gaussian prime, or the character of 2 or 1+i. That the label '2h' denotes such a count is my inference.

(2) Middle, labelled '2h-i-k'. There are a few lattice points (circles and dots) and two broken polygonal lines. Each is hatched on one side, the usual way to show which side is the interior of a region. One line has a convex corner and the other a reflex corner. The label 2h-i-k suggests the total count is being corrected by boundary or corner terms i and k. That would be a weighting of boundary lattice points by the local shape of the boundary, as in boundary corrections to area-by-lattice-points formulas (Pick-type) or to the half-weights in Eisenstein-type counts. This is my interpretation; the page does not state it.

(3) Bottom. Several hatched configurations sit among circles, dots and crosses:
- a horizontal hatched line crossed by short perpendicular hatched segments, i.e. boundary lines passing through lattice points;
- a double chevron (zigzag) with hatched arms meeting at points on a horizontal line;
- a small right-angle corner with hatching.
These look like a case list of how a region boundary can pass through or turn at a lattice point, with the hatching showing the interior side. They would be used to decide what fraction of a boundary point to count (1/2 on a straight side, angle-dependent at corners).

(4) Left margin. Calligraphic pen trials: Fraktur/script capitals P, A, B, L and a script 'L', the number 43 over 'A', and a word like 'Schola[r]'. They have no mathematical content. The previous page (33r) is unrelated: a geodetic station adjustment of angles with iterative (Gauss-Seidel-type) elimination of corrections a, b, c, d.

No formula on this page can be checked step by step. The page is preparatory geometric work for the lattice-point arguments developed on folio 34.

Corner-weight sketches hint at Pick-type boundary bookkeeping, but nothing explicit is stated, so no specific new result can be attributed.

checkable.asserts: 5+8i (the example on the next folio) has prime norm 89, so it is a Gaussian prime.
The norm 89 is congruent to 1 mod 8, the case relevant to biquadratic characters of 2 and 1+i.
5/8(p-1) with p=89 equals 55. This matches the '55' written next to 5+8i on the next folio, so the formula 5/8(p-1)+1/2(A-B) was evaluated for p=89.

transcription_corrections: The left-margin letters (P, A, B, L, script L, '43 A', 'Schola[r]?') are calligraphic pen trials, not mathematical symbols.

The top lattice has circles only at alternate points of alternate rows, with dots elsewhere: a sublattice of circles inside a lattice of dots, not simply 'rows of circles alternating with rows of dots'.
The two triangles in the top diagram are nearly congruent, one translated by roughly half a lattice step relative to the other.
Crosses ('x') also appear among the lattice markers in the bottom-left hatched diagram.
